item.title: On a Box Without an NVIDIA Card, I Tore NVIDIA's Closed Network Apart Down to the Bone
item.description: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural rendering network was reimplemented in pure Vulkan, byte-exact at all 75 block boundaries. My machine has no NVIDIA card, so I can't verify the signature GPU-side bit-exact parity. But I shallow-cloned the repo, read the source, cross-checked the 71-block graph, and actually ran one PTX divider regression on my own box — I tore it apart as far as I could tear it, said what I can say, and wrote down flat what I can't.

item.title: Reverse Engineering Claude Code's API Request Signing
item.description: An in-depth reverse engineering analysis of Claude Code's API request signing mechanism, revealing how the cch hash and xxHash64 are implemented, the secrets of Bun's runtime, and how Anthropic protects API calls with native code.

item.title: Neural Network Reverse Engineering: When Machine Learning Becomes a Puzzle Game
item.description: Jane Street released a special ML puzzle: given the complete neural network weights, find an input that makes it output non-zero. This isn't a typical black-box attack - it requires truly understanding what the network is computing. A college student spent days, going from linear programming to SAT solvers, and finally discovered the network was hiding an MD5 hash function.
